sections.title: Single node: leases, watches and durability

stages.name: Lamport clocks
hints: Topic `lamport`: keep one counter per process and hand it out with `send`
A local event and a send both increment the counter before it is used
On receive the counter becomes max(local, received) + 1 — the +1 is the whole point
Counters never go backwards, even when a message arrives from the past

tests.name: a fresh process has not ticked yet
a local event moves the clock on by one
a send stamps the counter it has just moved
a receive takes the maximum plus one
a receive never moves the clock backwards
reading the clock does not move it
each process keeps a counter of its own
an exchange orders cause before effect
a message from far in the future drags the clock with it
a long seeded exchange matches the tester's own replay

stages.name: Vector clocks and causal comparison
hints: Topic `vector-clock`: a map from process name to counter, and a missing entry is a zero
`cmp` answers before, after, equal or concurrent — four cases, not three
Merging on receive takes the componentwise maximum, then increments the receiver's own entry
Two clocks are concurrent when neither dominates: test both directions

tests.name: a process that has done nothing has an empty clock
a local event moves only the entry of the process that acted
a receive merges componentwise and then increments the receiver
a name nobody mentions counts as zero
cmp names all four relations
a clock is equal to itself
before and after are mirrors, and concurrent is symmetric
a delivered message is strictly behind the clock that received it
a merge never lowers a component
every pair of a seeded exchange agrees with the oracle

stages.name: Version vectors and sibling detection
hints: Topic `version-vector`: a value carries the vector of the replica that wrote it
A write that does not dominate an existing value creates a sibling instead of replacing it
Sync merges both replicas' sets and drops any value dominated by another
Siblings come back sorted so two replicas that agree answer identically

tests.name: a first write stamps the writing replica, and nothing else
a second write on the same replica replaces the first
two replicas writing apart fork into siblings
a sync leaves both replicas holding the same set
siblings come back sorted and deduplicated
a write that has seen every sibling replaces them all
put-ctx naming the whole context collapses the siblings
put-ctx naming a stale context forks again
a fresh process shares nothing with the one before it
a three-way fork keeps all three values

stages.name: Hybrid logical clocks
hints: Topic `hlc`: a timestamp is (l, c) — a physical part and a counter that breaks ties
`now` takes l = max(l, wall); when l did not move, c increments, otherwise c resets to 0
`recv` takes l = max(l, l_local, l_msg) and picks c from whichever source it matched
The result must be strictly greater than both the local clock and the message's

tests.name: a fresh clock takes the wall clock it is handed
the counter counts a stall and resets when the physical part moves
a wall clock that goes backwards never drags the clock back
reading the clock does not move it
a receive adopts a message from the future
a receive of a stale message keeps the local physical part
equal physical parts take the larger counter plus one
each process carries its own pair
a receive dominates both the local clock and the message
a seeded sequence is strictly increasing in (l, c)

stages.name: Consistent hashing with virtual nodes
hints: Topic `consistent-hash`: place `vnodes` points per node on a ring and walk clockwise
`locate` is a function: the same key must always answer the same node
Virtual nodes are what makes the load even — one point per node is visibly lumpy
`stats` reports how many of the sampled keys landed on each node

tests.name: a key always lands on the same node
a key only ever lands on a node that is on the ring
one node owns every key
the answer does not drift while the ring stands still
virtual nodes spread the keys evenly
one point per node is visibly lumpier
stats counts every sampled key exactly once
an empty ring answers instead of crashing
removing a node that was never added leaves the ring alone

stages.name: Key movement when the ring changes
hints: Adding a node may only take keys, never shuffle keys between two nodes that stayed
Removing a node may only give its keys away; everything else stays put
Roughly 1/N of the keys move when the Nth node joins — that is the whole point
Re-adding a node that was removed must restore the mapping exactly

tests.name: adding a node never shuffles keys between the nodes that stayed
every key that moves when a node joins moves to that node
removing a node only moves the keys it owned
roughly one key in N moves when the Nth node joins
removing a node and adding it back restores the mapping exactly
three joins in a row still never shuffle a key between survivors
a node leaving and a node joining only touch their own keys
the order the nodes joined in does not change where a key lands

stages.name: Rendezvous (HRW) hashing
hints: Topic `rendezvous`: score every node for the key and take the highest
No ring and no virtual nodes: the score function does all the work
`locate-k` returns the top k in score order, and its head is what `locate` answers
Removing a node only moves the keys it owned, exactly as a ring does

tests.name: the head of locate-k is what locate answers
locate-k ranks every node once, with no repeats
asking for more nodes than there are returns every one
the same key ranks the nodes the same way every time
one node owns every key
adding a node only takes keys, it never shuffles them
removing a node only moves the keys it owned
removing the best node promotes the runner-up
removing a node leaves the others in the same order
locating with no nodes answers instead of crashing

stages.name: Quorum math: N, R, W and overlap
hints: Topic `quorum`: a read and a write quorum overlap when R + W > N
Two writes can conflict when 2W <= N — that is a different question from overlap
The smallest read quorum that always sees the latest write is N - W + 1
Answer for the numbers you were given, not for the defaults

tests.name: a read and a write overlap exactly when R + W is more than N
two writes can conflict exactly when 2W is at most N
the smallest read quorum is N - W + 1
the three-replica settings everyone quotes
the edges: reading from nobody, writing to everybody, a single replica
a seeded sweep of larger triples agrees with the arithmetic
a larger read quorum never loses an overlap it already had
the same triple always gets the same answer

stages.name: Sloppy quorums and hinted handoff
hints: A sloppy quorum accepts a write on a node outside the preference list when a member is down
The stand-in records a hint naming the node the write really belongs to
When the real owner comes back, the hint is handed off and then forgotten
A sloppy quorum is not a quorum: it can lose the overlap guarantee, and must say so

tests.name: a write with every replica alive needs no stand-in
a write with a member down is accepted on a stand-in
the number of hints is exactly the number of replicas that were down
strict is false exactly when a stand-in was used
hints lists the keys a stand-in is holding
a handoff delivers every hint and leaves none
handing off twice delivers nothing the second time
a hint for an owner that never comes back is still held
an owner nobody hinted for is holding nothing

stages.name: Bloom filter
hints: Topic `bloom`: k hash positions per item over m bits, all set on add
`contains` is only ever 'maybe' or 'no': a false negative is a bug, never a tuning issue
The measured false-positive rate must sit inside the theoretical bound for m, k and n
Derive the k positions from one or two hashes; k independent hash functions are not needed

tests.name: init reports back the size it was given
an item that was added is always maybe
items that were never added are mostly not present
a false positive rate inside the theoretical bound
set bits grow with insertions and never exceed the filter
a filter with too few bits is useless but never loses an item
init a second time resets the filter
adding the same item twice changes nothing
the optimal number of hashes beats a badly chosen one

stages.name: HyperLogLog
hints: Topic `hll`: 2^p registers, each holding the longest run of leading zeros it has seen
The estimate is the harmonic mean of the registers, times alpha times m squared
Small cardinalities need linear counting, or the estimate is badly wrong
The relative error must sit inside 1.04 / sqrt(2^p) over many trials

tests.name: count on an empty sketch is zero
init reports two to the power p registers
the estimate of a small set is close to exact
adding the same item a thousand times does not change the estimate
counting twice gives the same answer
the insertion order does not change the estimate
a mean relative error inside the standard-error envelope
a larger precision is not worse than a smaller one
init a second time resets the sketch

stages.name: Merkle tree build
hints: Topic `merkle`: leaf = sha256(0x00 || leaf bytes), node = sha256(0x01 || left hex || right hex)
An odd node at a level is carried up unchanged, not duplicated
The root changes when any leaf changes, and only then
The same leaves always produce the same root, whatever order they were added in

tests.name: the root of four leaves is the one the oracle computes
a tree of one leaf is that leaf's hash
the root of an empty tree is the hash of nothing
an odd number of leaves carries the last node up
level zero holds the leaf hashes
the top level holds the root
changing one leaf changes the root and nothing else
the same leaves always give the same root
trees of every size up to seventeen match the oracle
every node of every level matches the oracle

stages.name: Merkle diff with the fewest round trips
hints: Compare roots first: equal roots mean equal trees and no further work
Descend only into subtrees whose hashes differ — that is the whole saving
Report the differing leaves as ranges, so a caller can fetch them in one go
Count the nodes you compared: a walk that visits everything has learnt nothing

tests.name: two identical trees diff to no ranges at all
diffing a tree against itself costs one comparison
one differing leaf is found exactly
adjacent differing leaves merge into one range
scattered differences match the ranges the oracle computes
a diff never looks at every node in the tree
a large tree with two scattered differences is still cheap
the diff is the same in both directions
two trees that differ everywhere report one whole range

stages.name: G-Counter and PN-Counter
hints: Topics `g-counter` and `pn-counter`: one entry per replica, merged by maximum
A PN-Counter is two G-Counters: increments and decrements, never one signed number
Merge must be commutative, associative and idempotent — every delivery order converges
A replica only ever writes its own entry; it copies others by taking the maximum

tests.name: a fresh counter reads zero and then counts up
the value is the sum over every replica
a stale merge never lowers the value
merging the same state twice changes nothing
a replica writes only its own entry, so no increment is lost
every delivery order of the same updates converges
a pn-counter keeps increments and decrements apart
a pn-counter can go below zero
every delivery order of increments and decrements converges

stages.name: LWW-Register and OR-Set
hints: Topic `lww-register`: value plus timestamp, and a deterministic tie-break on equal timestamps
Topic `or-set`: an add carries a unique tag; a remove takes away the tags it saw
An add concurrent with a remove survives — that is the whole difference from a 2P-Set
Re-adding after a remove must work, which is why tags cannot be reused

tests.name: an untouched register reads null
a set answers with the value it now holds
the larger timestamp wins whichever order the merges arrive in
equal timestamps break by replica name, so two replicas agree
every delivery order of register writes converges
elements come back sorted and without duplicates
an add concurrent with a remove survives
re-adding after a remove works, and a stale state cannot undo it
every delivery order of a mixed add and remove exchange converges

stages.name: RGA: a replicated sequence
hints: Topic `rga`: every element has an id and points at the element it was inserted after
Concurrent inserts at the same position are ordered by id, consistently on every replica
A delete leaves a tombstone: later inserts may still point at it
Every delivery order of the same operations must read back the same sequence

tests.name: a sequence builds up as it is typed
inserting after root prepends
a delete takes the character out of the text
an insert after a deleted element still lands in its place
two replicas inserting at the same position converge
both replicas read back the same sequence after a longer exchange
a tombstone survives a state that predates the delete
every delivery order of inserts and deletes converges

stages.name: Chandy-Lamport snapshots
hints: Topic `snapshot`: a process records its own state when it first sees a marker
After that it records every message arriving on a channel until that channel's marker
The snapshot's total must equal the system's total, whatever the interleaving
A process sends a marker on every outgoing channel immediately after recording

tests.name: a snapshot of a quiet system is the state the system is in
a snapshot taken while money is in flight still totals correctly
a process records its own state the first time it sees a marker and not again
a message arriving after its channel's marker is not recorded
a snapshot is complete only once every process and channel has reported
a seeded interleaving snapshots the same total every time
two snapshots in a row both total correctly
a marker started anywhere goes round a one-way ring
the reported total is the recorded balances plus the recorded channels

stages.name: Causal broadcast delivery order
hints: Topic `causal-broadcast`: a message carries the sender's vector clock
Deliver only when the message is the sender's next, and its other entries are already seen
Anything else waits in a buffer and is re-checked after every delivery
Delivering a message out of causal order is the failure this stage looks for

tests.name: a message whose dependency has not arrived is buffered, not delivered
filling the gap releases the buffered message at once
a sender's own messages are never delivered out of order
every delivery order satisfies the causal rule
a message that has already been delivered is not delivered twice
a seeded reordering of a causal chain still delivers in causal order
a broadcast stamps the sender's own entry and nothing else
two concurrent messages may be delivered in either order
a chain delivered in the order it was created never buffers anything

stages.name: Token bucket and leaky bucket
hints: Topic `token-bucket`: refill rate * elapsed, capped at the burst, then spend
Topic `leaky-bucket`: drain rate * elapsed, then refuse whatever would overflow
Time arrives with every command: never read a clock of your own
A long idle period fills the token bucket to the burst and no further

tests.name: a full bucket allows exactly the burst at time zero
the bucket refills at its rate and no faster
a bucket that has idled holds exactly the burst
a seeded sequence of takes matches the oracle step by step
fractional refills accumulate instead of being truncated
the same instant twice means no time has passed
a timestamp that goes backwards adds no tokens
the leaky bucket refuses what would overflow and takes it once it has drained
a seeded sequence of offers matches the leaky bucket oracle step by step

stages.name: Backoff, phi-accrual and SWIM suspicion
hints: Topic `backoff`: full jitter is uniform(0, min(cap, base * 2^attempt))
Topic `phi-accrual`: phi rises with the time since the last heartbeat, smoothly
Topic `swim`: alive, then suspect, then dead — two deadlines, both sharp
The sampled value arrives with the command, so a jittered delay is still reproducible

tests.name: a sweep of attempts and samples matches the full jitter formula
the cap holds however many attempts have failed
a seeded sample is never negative and never above the ceiling
phi never falls as the silence grows
phi stays well under one while the heartbeats keep coming
phi passes four once ten intervals have gone by
swim moves from alive to suspect to dead as the oracle says
both deadlines are sharp at the exact instant they fall
an ack moves a suspect node back to alive

stages.name: Bind, /version and /health
hints: Listen on the --listen-client-urls address and answer HTTP/1.1 on it
GET /version answers {"etcdserver":..,"etcdcluster":..} and GET /health {"health":"true"}
Keep the connection alive: the suite reuses one connection for thousands of requests
An unknown path is 404, and a GET on a POST-only endpoint is not a 200

tests.name: GET /version answers both version strings
GET /health says the node is healthy
an unknown path is a 404, not an empty 200
a refused path leaves the connection usable
a GET on a POST-only endpoint is not a 200
fifty requests in a row are all answered
a body that is not JSON is refused, and the node keeps serving
the status endpoint reports a version, a member id and a revision

stages.name: Put and the response header
hints: POST /v3/kv/put with base64 key and value, answering a header
Every write increments the store revision by one, and the header reports the new value
64-bit numbers are JSON strings; a field at its zero value may be left out entirely
raft_term is in the header too, and it never goes backwards

tests.name: a put answers with a header
the revision increases by exactly one
the revision is the same for every member id
writing the same key again still moves the revision
an empty value is a value
a key with awkward bytes survives the round trip
a large value is stored whole
many writes produce one increasing sequence
the header travels on every endpoint

stages.name: Range: reading one key
hints: POST /v3/kv/range with just a key is a point read
A key that is not there answers no kvs and count 0 — not an error
create_revision is set once, mod_revision moves with every put, version counts the puts
count is the number of keys the range holds, whatever limit was asked for

tests.name: a key that was never written is not an error
a key that was written reads back with its revisions
version counts the puts since the key was created
create_revision never moves while mod_revision does
the revision of a read is at least the revision of the write
a key holding an empty value is still one key

a point read is exact, not a prefix

stages.name: Ranges, prefixes and the whole store
hints: range_end makes the request a half-open range [key, range_end)
A prefix range ends at the key with its last byte incremented
key and range_end both � means every key in the store
Results come back in key order, which is byte order, not string order

tests.name: range_end is excluded, because the range is half-open
a prefix range takes everything under the prefix
a prefix range stops at the prefix boundary
a zero byte at both ends is every key in the store

stages.name: limit, sort order, count_only and keys_only
hints: limit cuts the answer and sets more, but never changes count
sort_order and sort_target together decide the order; the default is ascending by key
count_only answers the count and no kvs at all
keys_only answers the kvs with their values left out, not with empty values invented

tests.name: a limit cuts the answer but never the count
a limit as large as the range leaves more false

stages.name: MVCC: reading at a past revision
hints: revision in a range request reads the store as it was at that revision
A key deleted later is still there when read at a revision before the delete
The header of a historical read still reports the store's current revision
Revision 0 means 'now', because 0 is the zero value and cannot mean 'the beginning'

tests.name: a read at an old revision sees the old value
a key deleted later is still there before the delete
a key created later is absent before its creation
the header of a historical read reports the current revision
revision zero means now
a revision the store has not reached is an error

stages.name: prev_kv and deleting ranges
hints: prev_kv on a put answers the pair as it was before the write, or nothing when it is new
POST /v3/kv/deleterange answers how many keys it removed
A delete over a range removes every key in it and counts them all
Deleting a key that is not there is a successful request that deleted zero keys

tests.name: prev_kv on a put of a key that existed answers the old pair
prev_kv on a put of a new key answers nothing
a delete answers how many keys it removed

stages.name: Transactions: compare, success, failure
hints: POST /v3/kv/txn runs the success branch when every comparison holds, the failure one otherwise
succeeded is false when the failure branch ran, and may be omitted rather than sent as false
responses carries one entry per operation of the branch that ran, in order
A transaction is one atomic step: its writes share one revision

tests.name: a transaction with no comparisons succeeds

a comparison that does not hold runs the failure branch
responses carries one entry per operation, in order
two puts in one transaction share one revision
every comparison has to hold

stages.name: Compare-and-swap semantics
hints: VERSION = 0 is how you say 'this key does not exist'
CREATE, MOD, VALUE and VERSION are four different comparisons with four different fields
Two concurrent swaps from the same value: exactly one may succeed
A comparison naming a key that does not exist compares against zeros, it does not fail the request

tests.name: a create-if-absent transaction succeeds exactly once

stages.name: Compaction and ErrCompacted
hints: POST /v3/kv/compaction drops every revision below the one given
A read below the compacted revision is code 11, not an empty answer
Compaction never removes the newest version of a live key
Compacting twice, or below what is already compacted, is an error, not a no-op

stages.name: Leases: grant, attach, expire, revoke
hints: POST /v3/lease/grant answers an ID and the TTL it settled on
A put naming a lease binds the key to it; the kv answers with that lease id
When the lease expires every key attached to it disappears in one revision
Revoking is the same thing on demand, and revoking twice is an error

stages.name: Lease keepalive and TTL
hints: POST /v3/lease/keepalive is a stream: the answer is wrapped in {"result": ...}
A keepalive resets the lease's remaining time to its TTL
A keepalive for a lease that is gone answers TTL 0, not an error

stages.name: Watches
hints: POST /v3/watch is a stream: every message is a line of JSON wrapped in {"result": ...}
The first message acknowledges the create request and carries created: true
start_revision replays everything from that revision onwards, in revision order
A delete event carries type DELETE and a kv with only the key and mod_revision

stages.name: Error responses
hints: Errors are a 4xx status and a body of {"code": <grpc code>, "message": "..."}

An unknown path is 404 and never a 200 with an empty body
A bad request must not change the store, and must not close the connection

stages.name: Durability across SIGKILL
hints: An acknowledged write must survive kill -9 and a restart: fsync before you answer
The data directory must be reopenable without being reformatted
The revision sequence continues where it left off; it never restarts at 1

stages.name: A cluster forms and elects one leader
hints: --initial-cluster lists every member as name=peer-url, and every member gets the same list
